Typical applications for detouring or diverting road users on two-lane highways are shown in Figures 6P-7, 6P-8, and 6P-9. Channelizing devices and pavement markings are used to indicate the transition to the temporary roadway. items.title: Work within the Traveled Way of a Freeway or Expressway
items.source_excerpt: Support: 01 Special conditions encountered where vehicular traffic must be moved through or around TTC zones on high- speed, high-volume roadways can pose challenges to the TTC. Although the general principles outlined in other Sections of this Manual are applicable to all types of highways, high-speed, access-controlled highways need special planning and attention in order to accommodate vehicular traffic while also protecting road users and workers. The traffic volumes, vehicle mix (buses, trucks, cars, and bicycles, if permitted), and speed of vehicles on these facilities require that careful TTC procedures be implemented, for example, to induce critical merging maneuvers well in advance of work spaces and in a manner that creates minimum turbulence and delay in the vehicular traffic stream. 02 When the roadway capacity is reduced as a result of lane closures, the demand might exceed the available capacity and result in either a lengthy stopped or slow moving queue of vehicles that might extend past the normal signs used in the typical advance warning area. items.title: Work in the Vicinity of a Grade Crossing
items.source_excerpt: Standard: 01 When grade crossings exist either within or in the vicinity of a TTC zone, lane restrictions, flagging, or other operations shall not create conditions where vehicles can be queued across the tracks. If the queuing of vehicles across the tracks cannot be avoided, a uniformed law enforcement officer or flagger shall be provided at the crossing to prevent vehicles from stopping on the tracks, even if automatic warning devices are in place. Support: 02 Figure 6P-46 shows work in the vicinity of a grade crossing. 03 Section 8A.13 contains additional information regarding TTC zones in the vicinity of grade crossings. Guidance: 04 Early coordination with the railroad company or transit agency should occur before work starts.

items.title: Median Crossover for an Exit Ramp
items.source_excerpt: Guidance: 1. This typical application should be used for carrying an exit ramp across a closed directional roadway of a divided highway. The design criteria contained in the “AASHTO Green Book – A Policy On Geometric Design Of Highways And Streets,” 7th Edition, 2018, AASHTO should be used for determining the curved alignment. 2. The guide signs should indicate that the ramp is open, and where the temporary ramp is located. Conversely, if the ramp is closed, guide signs should indicate that the ramp is closed. 3. items.title: Work Affecting Pedestrian and Bicycle Facilities
items.source_excerpt: Support: 01 It is not uncommon, particularly in urban areas, that road work and the associated TTC will affect existing pedestrian or bicycle facilities. It is essential that the needs of all road users, including pedestrians with disabilities, are considered in TTC zones. 02 In addition to specific provisions identified in Sections 6N.05 through 6N.13, there are a number of provisions that might be applicable for all of the types of activities identified in this Chapter. Guidance: 03 Where pedestrian or bicyclist usage is high, the typical applications should be modified by giving particular attention to the provisions set forth in Chapter 6C, this Chapter, Sections 6K.02 and 6M.04, and in other Sections of Part 6 related to accessibility and detectability provisions in TTC zones. 04 Pedestrians should be separated from the worksite by appropriate devices that maintain the accessibility and detectability for pedestrians with disabilities. 05 Bicyclists and pedestrians should not be exposed to unprotected excavations, open utility access, overhanging equipment, or other such conditions. items.source_excerpt: Support: 01 Chapter 6C and Sections 6M.04 and 6N.04 contain additional information regarding the steps to follow when pedestrian or bicycle facilities are affected by the worksite. 02 In urban TTC zones, decisions are needed on how to control vehicular traffic, such as how many lanes are required, whether any turns need to be prohibited at intersections, and how to maintain access to business, industrial, and residential areas. 03 Pedestrian traffic needs separate attention. items.title: Typical Applications
items.source_excerpt: Support: 01 Chapter 6N contains discussions of typical TTC activities. Section 6A.02 contains discussions on development of TTC plans for the various activities. This Chapter presents typical applications for a variety of situations commonly encountered. While not every situation is addressed, the information illustrated can generally be adapted to a broad range of conditions. In many instances, an appropriate TTC plan is achieved by combining features from various typical applications. For example, work at an intersection might present a near-side TTC zone for one street and a far-side TTC zone for the other street. These treatments are found in two different typical applications, while a third typical application shows how to handle pedestrian crosswalk closures. 02 In general, the procedures illustrated represent minimum solutions for the situations depicted. items.title: Work Outside of the Shoulder
items.source_excerpt: Support: 01 When work is being performed beyond the shoulders, but within the right-of-way, little or no TTC might be needed. TTC generally is not needed where work is confined to an area 15 feet or more from the edge of the traveled way. However, TTC is appropriate where distracting situations exist, such as vehicles parked on the shoulder, vehicles accessing the worksite via the highway, and equipment traveling on or crossing the roadway to perform the work operations (for example, mowing). A typical application for work beyond the shoulder is shown in Figure 6P-1. items.title: Work within the Traveled Way at an Intersection

For example, work in one quadrant often creates a near-side work space on one street and a far-side work space on the cross street. items.title: Work Beyond the Shoulder
items.source_excerpt: Guidance: 1. If the work space is in the median of a divided highway, an advance warning sign should also be placed on the left-hand side of the directional roadway. Option: 2. The ROAD WORK AHEAD sign may be replaced with other appropriate signs such as the SHOULDER WORK sign. The SHOULDER WORK sign may be used for work adjacent to the shoulder. 3. The ROAD WORK AHEAD sign may be omitted where the work space is behind a barrier, more than 24 inches behind the curb, or 15 feet or more from the edge of any roadway. 4. For short-term, short-duration or mobile operation, all signs and channelizing devices may be eliminated if a vehicle with activated high-intensity rotating, flashing, oscillating, or strobe lights is used. 5. Vehicle hazard warning signals may be used to supplement high-intensity rotating, flashing, oscillating, or strobe lights. Standard: 6. Vehicle hazard warning signals shall not be used instead of the vehicle’s high-intensity rotating, flashing, oscillating, or strobe lights. source_unit_metadata.title: Road Closure with an Off-Site Detour

items.subject: Regulatory traffic control devices
items.threshold: Regulatory traffic control devices should be modified as needed for the duration of the detour.
items.source_span: Regulatory traffic control devices should be modified as needed for the duration of the detour.

items.subject: A Route Sign Directional assembly
items.threshold: A Route Sign Directional assembly may be placed on the far left corner of the intersection to augment or replace the one shown on the near right corner.
items.source_span: A Route Sign Directional assembly may be placed on the far left corner of the intersection to augment or replace the one shown on the near right corner.

items.subject: Cardinal direction plaques
items.threshold: Cardinal direction plaques may be used with route signs. Sect. 6P.01 December 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition Page 875
items.source_span: Cardinal direction plaques may be used with route signs. Sect. 6P.01 December 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition Page 875

items.subject: Signs and object markers are shown for one direction of travel only.
items.threshold: Signs and object markers are shown for one direction of travel only.
items.source_span: Signs and object markers are shown for one direction of travel only.

items.subject: Devices similar to those depicted
items.threshold: Devices similar to those depicted shall be placed for the opposite direction of travel.
items.source_span: Devices similar to those depicted shall be placed for the opposite direction of travel.

items.subject: Pavement markings no longer applicable to the traffic pattern of the roadway
items.threshold: Pavement markings no longer applicable to the traffic pattern of the roadway shall be removed or obliterated before any new traffic patterns are open to traffic.
items.source_span: Pavement markings no longer applicable to the traffic pattern of the roadway shall be removed or obliterated before any new traffic patterns are open to traffic.

items.subject: Temporary traffic barriers and end treatments
items.threshold: Temporary traffic barriers and end treatments shall be crashworthy.
items.source_span: Temporary traffic barriers and end treatments shall be crashworthy.

items.subject: If the tangent distance along the temporary diversion is more than 600 feet, a Reverse Curve sign, left first,
items.threshold: If the tangent distance along the temporary diversion is more than 600 feet, a Reverse Curve sign, left first, should be used instead of the Double Reverse Curve sign, and a second Reverse Curve sign, right first, should be placed in advance of the second reverse curve back to the original alignment.
items.source_span: If the tangent distance along the temporary diversion is more than 600 feet, a Reverse Curve sign, left first, should be used instead of the Double Reverse Curve sign, and a second Reverse Curve sign, right first, should be placed in advance of the second reverse curve back to the original alignment.

items.subject: When the tangent section of the diversion is more than 600 feet, and the diversion has sharp curves with recommended speeds of 30 mph or less, Reverse Turn signs
items.threshold: When the tangent section of the diversion is more than 600 feet, and the diversion has sharp curves with recommended speeds of 30 mph or less, Reverse Turn signs should be used.
items.source_span: When the tangent section of the diversion is more than 600 feet, and the diversion has sharp curves with recommended speeds of 30 mph or less, Reverse Turn signs should be used.

items.subject: Where the temporary pavement and old pavement are different colors, the temporary pavement
items.threshold: Where the temporary pavement and old pavement are different colors, the temporary pavement should start on the tangent of the existing pavement and end on the tangent of the existing pavement.
items.source_span: Where the temporary pavement and old pavement are different colors, the temporary pavement should start on the tangent of the existing pavement and end on the tangent of the existing pavement.

items.subject: Delineators or channelizing devices
items.threshold: Delineators or channelizing devices should be used along the diversion.
items.source_span: Delineators or channelizing devices should be used along the diversion.

items.subject: Flashing warning lights and/or flags
items.threshold: Flashing warning lights and/or flags may be used to call attention to the warning signs.
items.source_span: Flashing warning lights and/or flags may be used to call attention to the warning signs.

items.subject: On sharp curves, large arrow signs
items.threshold: On sharp curves, large arrow signs may be used in addition to other advance warning signs. Sect. 6P.01 December 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition Page 873 Known
items.source_span: On sharp curves, large arrow signs may be used in addition to other advance warning signs. Sect. 6P.01 December 2023 MUTCD 11th Edition Page 873 Known

items.threshold: A flagger or uniformed law enforcement officer shall be used for this application. The flagger, if used for this application, shall follow the procedures provided in Sections 6D.05 and 6D.06.
items.source_span: A flagger or uniformed law enforcement officer shall be used for this application. The flagger, if used for this application, shall follow the procedures provided in Sections 6D.05 and 6D.06.

items.threshold: The uniformed law enforcement officer, if used for this application, should follow the procedures provided in Sections 6D.05 and 6D.06.
items.source_span: The uniformed law enforcement officer, if used for this application, should follow the procedures provided in Sections 6D.05 and 6D.06.

items.subject: A BE PREPARED TO STOP sign
items.threshold: A BE PREPARED TO STOP sign may be added to the sign series.
items.source_span: A BE PREPARED TO STOP sign may be added to the sign series.

items.subject: Positive protection devices
items.threshold: Positive protection devices may be used per Section 6M.02.
items.source_span: Positive protection devices may be used per Section 6M.02.

items.subject: Automated Flagger Assistance Devices (see Section 6L.02)
items.threshold: Automated Flagger Assistance Devices (see Section 6L.02) may be used in situations where there is only one lane of approaching traffic in the direction to be controlled.
items.source_span: Automated Flagger Assistance Devices (see Section 6L.02) may be used in situations where there is only one lane of approaching traffic in the direction to be controlled.

items.subject: When used, the BE PREPARED TO STOP sign

source_unit_metadata.title: Lane Closure on the Near Side of an Intersection

items.subject: The merging taper
items.threshold: The merging taper shall direct vehicular traffic into either the right-hand or left-hand lane, but not both.
items.source_span: The merging taper shall direct vehicular traffic into either the right-hand or left-hand lane, but not both.

items.subject: In this typical application, a left taper
items.threshold: In this typical application, a left taper should be used so that right-turn movements will not impede through motor vehicle traffic. However, the reverse should be true for left-turn movements.
items.source_span: In this typical application, a left taper should be used so that right-turn movements will not impede through motor vehicle traffic. However, the reverse should be true for left-turn movements.

items.subject: If the work space extends across a crosswalk, the crosswalk
